assumptions: The February 2027 passport obligation and described scope take effect substantially as stated, although implementation guidance and the battery semantic catalogue may continue to change.

A customer can lawfully engage the venture for operational evidence review without the venture holding a certification credential, provided the service does not claim to transfer statutory responsibility or provide formal compliance assurance.
Target operators can authorize access to relevant supplier evidence and customer-controlled workspaces, but the availability, authenticity, and timeliness of that evidence remain uncertain.
The proposed prices are hypotheses rather than demonstrated market prices, and no repeat purchase or annual renewal is assumed.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several paid pilots with smaller covered operators should demonstrate that the acceptance sprint is purchased separately from passport platforms or certification work, quantify the avoided delay or rework, and report sales-cycle length, acquisition source and cost, delivery and exception hours, realized contribution margin, repeat events, and renewal behavior; at least one signed laboratory or adviser channel agreement and one customer workflow-integration agreement would materially strengthen the case.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Moving the intervention upstream to supplier or model approval is a coherent insight because incomplete evidence is cheaper to reject before launch work compounds. The regulatory trigger is real and the bounded, platform-neutral service is better focused than generic passport hosting, but the underlying need is visible to incumbents and public programs rather than proprietary.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A delayed or reworked market launch can create serious pain, and the responsible economic operator has a clear reason to seek complete evidence before approval. However, no target smaller operator has paid, budgeted, or quantified the loss, and buyers may expect an existing platform, certifier, supplier, or internal compliance function to perform the check.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Deposits, fixed scope, customer-hosted delivery, and avoidance of long-lived passport infrastructure make the model capital-light and improve cash conversion. Against that, pricing, CAC, delivery hours, exception frequency, liability cost, contribution margin, repeat demand, and renewal are all unmeasured; supplier chasing can destroy fixed-fee margin, and the stated wealth path requires an unproven scale of roughly one hundred meaningful accounts.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Smaller EU operators approaching approval of a covered battery supplier or model form a recognizable event-driven beachhead. Yet the packet does not establish how many reachable operators are both underserved and large enough to pay, and the inclusion of e-bike, e-scooter, storage, EV, and industrial operators makes the initial segment operationally broader than it first appears.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The pre-procurement and platform-neutral positioning could win occasional specialist engagements. A dominant position is unlikely on current evidence because Siemens, Minespider, and certifier-platform alliances already cover validation and upstream evidence work, while the operator retains the relationship, legal duty, data, and approval decision.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful first engagement could extend across additional suppliers, models, data changes, annual workflow support, adjacent battery categories, and EU geographies. Those adjacencies are plausible but do not yet become structurally easier through owned data, exclusive rights, or a demonstrated distribution engine, so expansion may remain service-by-service selling.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Customer-specific mappings, exception playbooks, and review history can improve delivery within an account. They provide limited durable protection because outputs must be portable, cross-customer data reuse is constrained, public guidance reduces schema scarcity, agreements are nonexclusive and revocable, and larger vendors can reproduce or bundle the workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A bounded, customer-hosted engagement offers neutrality, lower lock-in, and less operational burden than adopting another hosted platform solely for evidence readiness. The packet does not demonstrate that this is materially faster, cheaper, more trusted, or more accurate than incumbent readiness tools, certification partners, or internal work, especially once both sprint and support fees are included.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The February 2027 deadline, evolving guidance, and incomplete registry infrastructure create an unusually timely preparation window and force covered operators to confront data readiness. Some urgency may be temporary, while the same regulatory momentum is drawing capable incumbents and subsidized public tooling into the market.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Independent laboratories and import advisers are logically close to the triggering event, and targeted technical outreach is feasible without a personal-media brand. No partner willingness, lead volume, conversion, sales cycle, channel share, or CAC is evidenced; the strongest certifier route is already being occupied by established alliances, and the founder currently owns no customer relationship.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-lineage skills, EU context, low required capital, and ability to run one scoped pilot support initial execution. Reliable delivery still depends on regulatory interpretation, customer authorization, supplier cooperation, security, domain trust, professional-liability boundaries, and labor-intensive exception handling; concurrent work is unlikely to fit five hours daily without proven templates and delegated expertise.

highest_value_structural_change: Embed the acceptance check as a standard prerequisite inside an independent battery laboratory's or specialist import adviser's existing paid workflow under a durable preferred-channel or co-delivery agreement that defines referral ownership, evidence access, standardized scope, liability boundaries, and repeat triggers. This would turn speculative outreach into event-linked distribution and create a harder-to-bundle workflow position.
main_structural_strength: The redesign attaches a bounded, deposit-funded deliverable to a concrete pre-procurement decision and leaves data, platform choice, and statutory responsibility with the customer, avoiding the capital, longevity, and migration burden of operating a permanent passport platform.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that smaller operators will buy this check as a separate service at attractive contribution margins, and the venture lacks both an owned distribution channel and a defensible control point while well-resourced platforms and certifier alliances can bundle the same work.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Minespider publicly offers a EUR 11,900 annual small-team plan that already includes readiness checks, evidence storage, audit trail, integration, and unlimited passports and models, while Siemens and the Bureau Veritas-Circulor alliance cover overlapping validation and upstream evidence work; this directly challenges both stand-alone willingness to pay and differentiation.
